name: hive-mind
description: Visualizes code dependencies as an interactive Obsidian-style graph and provides Copilot tools to analyze change impact across your codebase.

chatParticipants.name: hivemind
chatParticipants.description: Ask about code dependencies, impact analysis, and related files

commands.name: impact
commands.description: Analyze which files are affected if the current file changes

commands.name: deps
commands.description: Show dependencies of the current file

commands.name: cycles
commands.description: Detect circular dependencies in the workspace

disambiguation.description: The user wants to understand code dependencies, imports, file relationships, or how files connect to each other in the codebase.
examples: What files does this file depend on?
What imports does this module have?
Which files are related to this one?

disambiguation.description: The user wants to know which files would be affected by changing a specific file, or wants to understand the downstream impact of a code change.
examples: What would break if I change this file?
Which files depend on this module?
What is the impact of modifying this code?
Show me what files I need to update if I change this

disambiguation.description: The user wants to find circular or cyclic dependencies in the codebase.
examples: Find import cycles in my project

hiveMind.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of source files to index. Increase for very large workspaces.

hiveMind.ignoredDirectories.description: Additional directory names to exclude from analysis (on top of the built-in list like node_modules, .git, dist, etc.).

hiveMind.externalDirectories.markdownDescription:
Directory names (or relative paths) containing external/third-party code that should be **indexed for import resolution** but **excluded from analysis outputs** (orphan counts, circular dependency detection, impact lists, dependency lists, etc.). Use this for directories like `extlib`, `thirdparty`, `external`, or OS-specific build imports that you don't modify.

Example: `["extlib", "thirdparty/windows", "thirdparty/linux"]`

hivemind.clangPath.description: Optional override path to a C/C++ compiler executable used by hivemind_macroExpand and hivemind_buildSubset. Accepts cl.exe (MSVC), g++/gcc, or clang/clang-cl. If empty, Hive Mind auto-detects: cl.exe on Windows, g++ on Linux/Mac, then clang as a fallback. Setting name kept for backwards compatibility.

hiveMind.respectIfdefBranches.description: When true, Hive Mind strips #include directives that lie in dead #ifdef/#if branches based on -D flags from compile_commands.json. Set to false to revert to the legacy behaviour of treating every #include as a real edge (more edges, more false-positive cycles, but no risk of dropping a real edge).

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getDependencies
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns all files that a given source file imports or depends on (direct and transitive). Use this ONLY when you need a specific depth-controlled dependency list and already have general context. DO NOT call this as your first tool — call hivemind_getContext instead, which includes dependencies plus much more. DO NOT use this to find what depends on a file (that's hivemind_getImpact). Prefer hivemind_planChange when planning a multi-file edit.

filePath.description: Path to the file — relative to workspace root or absolute. Fuzzy matching is supported (e.g. just the filename).

depth.description: Traversal depth. 1 = direct only, -1 = all transitive. Defaults to 2.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getImpact
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Given a file being modified, returns all files that import or transitively depend on it (downstream blast radius). Use ONLY for a focused reverse-dependency query with depth control. DO NOT call this as your first tool — hivemind_getContext already includes dependents. Prefer hivemind_planChange when planning multi-file changes (it scores and prioritizes the impacted files). DO NOT use this to find what a file imports (that's hivemind_getDependencies).

filePath.description: Path to the file being changed — relative to workspace root or absolute

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getRelatedFiles
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns direct imports AND direct dependents of a file in one call (1-hop both directions). Use ONLY when you need a quick bidirectional snapshot without depth traversal. DO NOT call this as your first tool — hivemind_getContext is strictly better (includes this data plus tests, co-changed files, and symbols). DO NOT use this for transitive analysis (use getDependencies or getImpact with depth > 1).

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getFullGraph
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a workspace-level architectural overview: hub files, language breakdown, edge counts, and cycle summary. Use this ONLY for high-level 'how is this codebase structured?' questions. DO NOT use for file-specific queries (use hivemind_getContext). DO NOT use to detect cycles in detail (use hivemind_detectCycles for the actual cycle chains).

maxNodes.description: Maximum number of nodes to return. Defaults to 150.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_detectCycles
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Detects and returns all circular dependency chains in the workspace with full cycle paths. Use when the user asks about circular imports, cyclic dependencies, or build-order issues. DO NOT confuse with hivemind_getFullGraph (which only reports a cycle count, not the actual chains).

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getTestFiles
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Given a source file, returns its associated test files (e.g. foo.test.ts for foo.ts), and vice versa. Use ONLY when you need the test mapping alone (e.g. 'which tests cover this file?'). DO NOT call this as your first tool — hivemind_getContext already includes test files. Prefer hivemind_planChange when planning edits (it includes tests in the plan).

filePath.description: Path to the source or test file

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_findSymbol
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches for a function, class, interface, type, or variable by name across all workspace files. Returns file locations and symbol kinds (definition sites). Use when you need to locate a symbol's definition file. DO NOT use this to find usages/references of a C/C++ symbol (use hivemind_findReferences). DO NOT use as your first tool when exploring a file — hivemind_getContext already includes exported symbols for the target file.

symbolName.description: The name of the symbol to search for (function, class, type, variable, etc.)

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_coChanged
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns files that frequently change together with the given file based on git commit history (temporal coupling). These are files that SHOULD be co-modified even without import relationships. Use ONLY when you specifically need git-history coupling data. DO NOT call this as your first tool — hivemind_getContext already includes co-changed files. Prefer hivemind_planChange for change planning (it factors co-change into its scoring).

filePath.description: Path to the file to find co-changed files for

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getContext
languageModelTools.modelDescription: THE RECOMMENDED FIRST TOOL. Returns a comprehensive context bundle for a file: dependencies, dependents, test files, co-changed files, and exported symbols — all in one call. ALWAYS call this first when starting work on any file. It replaces calling getDependencies, getImpact, getTestFiles, coChanged, and findSymbol separately — DO NOT call those individually unless you need deeper depth or specific filtering that getContext doesn't provide. After calling this, use hivemind_planChange if you need a prioritized edit plan.

filePath.description: Path to the file — relative to workspace root or absolute

task.description: Optional description of what you're trying to do. Helps frame the context.

includeContent.description: If true, includes the file's source code (capped at 200 lines). Default false.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_planChange
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Given a file and a description of intended changes, returns a PRIORITIZED edit plan: files to modify (scored), files to read for context, tests to run, and peripherally affected files. Combines structural deps + test relationships + git co-change history into a single ranked output. Use this BEFORE making any multi-file change. Superior to calling getImpact/getTestFiles/coChanged separately because it scores and categorizes. Requires a `description` of what you're changing — if you don't know the change yet, use hivemind_getContext first.

filePath.description: Path to the primary file being changed

description.description: What change is being made — e.g. 'rename the handleRequest method' or 'add a new parameter to the constructor'

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_search
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches the workspace for text or regex patterns, ranking results by dependency-graph structural signals (not just hit count). Boosts files whose graph neighbors also match, files near contextFile, and hub files. Use this for 'where is X used/referenced across the whole codebase?' questions. DO NOT confuse with hivemind_findSymbol (which finds definitions only) or hivemind_findReferences (which is C/C++-specific scope-aware reference finding). This tool works on ANY language and searches raw text.

query.description: The text or regex pattern to search for across all workspace files

isRegex.description: If true, treat query as a regular expression. Default false.

caseSensitive.description: If true, match case. Default false (case-insensitive).

maxResults.description: Maximum number of files to return. Default 30.

contextFile.description: Optional file path to bias results toward. Files structurally connected to this file get boosted in ranking.

includeSnippets.description: If true, include code snippets from top matches. Default true.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getCppPair
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Given a C/C++ file, returns the matching header/source/inline pair files (.h↔.cpp↔.inl). ALWAYS call this BEFORE editing any C++ file — the declaration in the header must stay in sync with the implementation. Only relevant for C/C++ files. DO NOT use for non-C/C++ languages. DO NOT confuse with hivemind_getDependencies (which shows all imports, not the header/source pair).

filePath.description: Path to a C/C++ file — relative to workspace root or absolute

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_findMacro
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Locates `#define` macro definitions across all C/C++ files. Returns ONLY the definition text (not usages). Use this to look up what a macro IS (its body text). DO NOT use this if you need the actual expanded result after preprocessing — use hivemind_macroExpand instead (it runs the real preprocessor and handles #ifdef, -D flags, and recursive expansion). DO NOT use this for non-macro symbols — use hivemind_findSymbol for functions/classes or hivemind_findReferences for usage sites.

name.description: Macro name to find (e.g. 'FCIMPL3', 'STATIC_CONTRACT_NOTHROW'). By default an exact match — set exact:false for substring search.

exact.description: If true (default), exact name match. If false, substring match — useful when you only know part of the macro name.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of definitions to return. Default 25.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_findReferences
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns every place a C/C++ symbol is referenced. Uses Hive Mind's tree-sitter index — comments, string literals, and dead #ifdef branches are stripped before matching. Each hit is tagged with a `confidence` (high/medium/low) reflecting how unique the name is across the workspace. Use this BEFORE renaming any C/C++ function, class, or variable — for `medium`/`low` confidence results verify each manually. Required: `symbolName`. `filePath` is accepted for compatibility but is not required. Position-only queries (`line`/`character`) are not supported in this build.

filePath.description: Path to a C/C++ file. Accepted for backwards-compatibility but not required — the tree-sitter resolver searches the entire workspace index.

symbolName.description: Name of the symbol to find references for (e.g. 'doFoo', 'MyClass::bar', 'kMaxSize'). Required — position-only lookup is not supported in this build.

line.description: Accepted for backwards-compatibility; ignored by the tree-sitter resolver.

character.description: Accepted for backwards-compatibility; ignored by the tree-sitter resolver.

includeDeclaration.description: If true (default), include the declaration site in results. Set false to see only call sites / usages.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of references to display. Default 100.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_findOverrides
languageModelTools.modelDescription: For a C/C++ virtual method, returns every concrete implementation across the codebase using the tree-sitter inheritance closure built during workspace indexing. Use BEFORE modifying a virtual method's signature, behavior contract, or visibility — every `high`-confidence override returned must be updated in lockstep; `medium`/`low` results should be sanity-checked. Closes the virtual-dispatch blind spot that text grep cannot solve. Required: `symbolName` (the method name).

filePath.description: Optional path to a C/C++ file. Accepted for backwards-compatibility; the resolver searches the workspace inheritance closure.

symbolName.description: Name of the virtual method (e.g. 'doWork', 'bar'). Required.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of overrides to display. Default 100.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_callHierarchy
languageModelTools.modelDescription: For a C/C++ function, returns who calls it (incoming) and/or what it calls (outgoing) using Hive Mind's tree-sitter call-edge index. Supports `depth: 2` to trace two levels in a single call (e.g. callers-of-callers). Use this when tracing bugs across function boundaries or before changing a function's signature/contract to understand the upstream and downstream blast radius. Required: `symbolName` (or qualified name like `MyClass::handle`).

filePath.description: Optional path to a C/C++ file. Accepted for backwards-compatibility; the resolver searches the workspace function index.

direction.description: incoming = who calls this | outgoing = what this calls | both (default).

depth.description: How many levels deep to trace (1 or 2). Default 1. Use 2 sparingly — output grows quickly.

maxPerLevel.description: Cap on number of children at each level. Default 25.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_typeHierarchy
languageModelTools.modelDescription: For a C/C++ class, struct, or interface, returns its supertypes (base classes) and/or subtypes (derived classes) using Hive Mind's tree-sitter inheritance index. Handles multiple inheritance. Use BEFORE modifying any base class — every subtype returned may be affected. Combine with `hivemind_findOverrides` on individual virtual methods to find concrete implementations to update. Required: `symbolName` (the class/struct/interface name).

filePath.description: Optional path to a C/C++ file. Accepted for backwards-compatibility; the resolver searches the workspace inheritance closure.

symbolName.description: Name of the class, struct, or interface (e.g. 'IFoo', 'BaseWidget'). Required.

depth.description: How many levels deep to trace (1, 2, or 3). Default 2.

maxPerLevel.description: Cap on number of children at each level. Default 25.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_macroExpand
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs the C/C++ preprocessor (`cl.exe /E` on Windows, `g++ -E` on Linux/Mac, with clang as a fallback) and returns the actual preprocessor expansion of a specific source line. Flag source priority: compile_commands.json entry → active project profile (e.g. the built-in Sage X3 profile) → workspace heuristics. Use this when you need to know what `FCIMPL3(MyMethod, ...)` (or any nested/conditional macro) ACTUALLY becomes in this specific translation unit — `hivemind_findMacro` only shows the #define text and cannot account for #ifdef branches, -D flags, or recursive expansion. Required: `filePath` (must be a .cpp/.cc/.cxx — not a header), `line` (1-indexed). Optional: `contextLines` (default 0; ±N lines around `line`).

filePath.description: Path to a C/C++ source file (.cpp/.cc/.cxx/.c). Headers are NOT supported — call this on a TU that #includes the header instead.

contextLines.description: Include ±N lines of expansion around the target line. Default 0. Cap 20.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds for the clang invocation. Default 30000.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_buildSubset
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs syntax-only compilation (`cl.exe /Zs` on Windows, `g++ -fsyntax-only` on Linux/Mac, with clang as a fallback) on every translation unit in the impact set of a seed file. Flag source priority: each TU's compile_commands.json entry → active project profile (e.g. the built-in Sage X3 profile). This is the cheapest way to answer 'did I break the build?' after editing a header — no codegen, no linking, no PDB locking. Returns pass/fail per TU plus compiler diagnostics. Required: `filePath` (the changed file). Optional: `maxTUs` (default 50, cap 500), `depth`, `perFileTimeoutMs`, `totalBudgetMs`, `parallelism`, `explicitTUs` (skip impact walk; compile exactly these TUs).

filePath.description: Seed file (the one changed). Reverse-dependency walk starts here.

maxTUs.description: Cap on number of translation units to compile. Default 50. Above 200 is unwise on large repos.

perFileTimeoutMs.description: Per-TU compiler timeout in milliseconds. Default 60000.

totalBudgetMs.description: Total wallclock budget in milliseconds. Default 300000 (5 min).

parallelism.description: Max concurrent compiler processes. Default min(8, CPU count).

explicitTUs.description: Optional explicit list of TUs to compile. Skips the impact-graph walk; only these files are checked.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_asanBuild
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compiles C/C++ file(s) with AddressSanitizer (`/fsanitize=address` on MSVC, `-fsanitize=address` on GCC/Clang) and optionally runs the resulting binary to capture runtime memory errors (heap-buffer-overflow, use-after-free, stack-buffer-overflow, memory leaks, etc.). Does NOT require any external install — ASan is built into modern compilers. Use this when investigating crashes, memory corruption, or validating a fix for a buffer-related bug. Requires: `filePath` (one or more .cpp/.c files, comma-separated). Optional: `sanitizers` ('address'|'undefined'|'address,undefined'), `runCommand` (binary to execute after compile), `runCwd`, `parallelism`. Returns compile diagnostics + structured sanitizer reports with file/line/function/stack trace. MSVC only supports 'address'. DO NOT confuse with hivemind_buildSubset (syntax-only check, no codegen, no ASan).

filePath.description: File(s) to compile with ASan. Comma-separated for multiple files. Workspace-relative or absolute paths.

sanitizers.description: Which sanitizers to enable. Default 'address'. MSVC only supports 'address'.

runCommand.description: Command to run the sanitized binary (e.g. path to test executable). If omitted, only compiles.

runCwd.description: Working directory for the run command. Defaults to workspace root.

parallelism.description: Max concurrent compiler processes. Default min(4, CPU count).

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getWarnings
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns compiler warnings and errors from the LOCAL VS Code Problems panel (IntelliSense, clang-tidy, MSVC diagnostics running in the IDE). Scoped to a file + its dependents when filePath is provided. Use this for LOCAL, real-time IDE diagnostics that update as you edit. DO NOT confuse with hivemind_getCIWarnings (which fetches from the remote GitHub Actions pipeline) or hivemind_getCodeQLAlerts (which is for static-analysis/security findings). This tool shows what the IDE sees RIGHT NOW.

filePath.description: Optional path to a C/C++ file. If supplied, results are limited to this file and all files that include it.

severity.description: Minimum severity to include. 'warning' (default) returns errors and warnings; 'all' returns everything including hints.

source.description: Optional filter by diagnostic source, e.g. 'MSVC', 'clang-tidy', 'C/C++'. Case-insensitive substring match.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getCodeQLAlerts
languageModelTools.displayName: Get CodeQL / SARIF Static Analysis Alerts
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns CodeQL and static analysis alerts (security vulnerabilities, code quality issues) from local SARIF files AND/OR the GitHub code-scanning API. Use this when the user asks about CodeQL findings, static analysis results, security alerts, or SARIF output. DO NOT confuse with hivemind_getWarnings (which is local IDE compiler diagnostics) or hivemind_getCIWarnings (which is build pipeline annotations like compiler errors/warnings from CI). This tool is specifically for STATIC ANALYSIS tools: CodeQL, clang-tidy SARIF, MSVC /analyze, etc.

sarifPath.description: Optional explicit path to a `.sarif` file, relative to workspace root or absolute. If omitted, Hive Mind searches common output locations.

ruleId.description: Optional rule filter, e.g. 'cpp/buffer-overflow' or just 'buffer'. Case-insensitive substring match.

filePath.description: Optional file path to restrict alerts to a single source file.

severity.description: Optional severity filter: 'error', 'warning', or 'note'. Case-insensitive substring match against the SARIF `level` field.

source.description: Where to look for alerts. 'local' = SARIF files in workspace, 'github' = GitHub code-scanning API, 'both' (default) = check both.

maxResults.description: Maximum alert rows to return. Default 50.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_getCIWarnings
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches build warnings, errors, and annotations from the REMOTE GitHub Actions CI pipeline (the latest completed workflow run). Use this when the user asks about CI failures, pipeline errors, build-breaking warnings, or 'why did the build fail?'. DO NOT confuse with hivemind_getWarnings (which is local IDE diagnostics) or hivemind_getCodeQLAlerts (which is static-analysis/security findings). This tool is specifically for GitHub Actions build output: compiler errors, linker failures, and check-run annotations from CI.

workflowFileName.description: Optional workflow file name (e.g. 'runtime-build.yml', 'ci.yml'). If omitted, uses the latest completed run across all workflows.

branch.description: Optional branch filter (e.g. 'main', 'develop'). If omitted, uses the latest run across all branches.

filePath.description: Optional file path to restrict annotations to a specific source file.

level.description: Filter by annotation level. 'all' (default) returns everything.

maxResults.description: Maximum annotation rows to return. Default 100.

languageModelTools.name: hivemind_unusedIncludes
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Analyzes a C/C++ file and reports which #include directives appear to be unused — i.e., no symbols exported by the included header are referenced in the source file. Uses tree-sitter parsing + identifier cross-referencing. Results are heuristic: macros, templates, and ADL can create invisible dependencies. ALWAYS verify removals with hivemind_buildSubset afterward. Use this when cleaning up headers, reducing compile times, or auditing include hygiene. Only works on C/C++ files. DO NOT confuse with hivemind_getDependencies (which shows resolved deps but doesn't tell you if they're actually used).

filePath.description: Path to a C/C++ file to analyze for unused includes.

confidence.description: 'high' = only report includes where we positively identified exported symbols AND none are used. 'all' (default) = also report unresolved/empty headers as 'likely-unused'.
